articles.subject: dashboard
articles.title: Why does the app not load, or only partly work offline?
articles.summary: Offline, only what you downloaded works, and live classes, the tutor, messages, progress and plans always need a connection.
body: If a page says This needs a connection, that part of Alimun only works online: live classes, the tutor, messages, progress and plans in Settings. It opens again by itself when you are back online.

Only what you downloaded works offline. Go to Settings, then Use Alimun offline, and check that each item says On this device; while you are online, press Download or Download all for anything missing. If a download stops, you see The download stopped. Check your connection and try again; trying again keeps what already arrived and carries on from there.
Without a plan, downloads hold only the free parts, so later units, texts and papers show Comes with a plan offline too.
If you do not see Use Alimun offline in Settings, the browser you are using cannot keep downloads; open your dashboard in another browser.

If a page does not load, you see a message such as The book did not load. Check your connection and try again. If Home says your data could not be loaded, press Try again. If it still does not work, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com, and tell us your device and browser.

articles.subject: teachers
articles.title: How do I apply to teach with Alimun, and what happens next?
articles.summary: You apply from the Careers page, then Alimun reviews your application, invites you to a short video call and, after a good call, to a free 30-minute trial class before approving you.
body: Press “Apply as teacher” on the Careers page. The form asks for the language you teach, your years of teaching experience, your specialty and a short bio that your students will see. You then create your teacher account with your name, email address, a password and the country you live in, and confirm your email address from the message we send you. You use this account to follow your application and, once approved, to teach.

While your application is being reviewed, your dashboard says “Your application is being reviewed”. We read every application ourselves. If we would like to meet you, we email you an invitation and your dashboard shows the free times for a video call with us of about 30 minutes, in your own time zone. Press a time, then press it again to confirm. You can change the time with “Change the time” until 12 hours before, and “Join the call” opens 10 minutes before it starts. The call is just you and us, and it is not recorded.

After a good call, the next step is a free 30-minute trial class with a few of our learners, so you can show us how you teach. We email you the time, and your dashboard shows it with “Check in” (from an hour before, and at least 5 minutes before the start, please) and “Join the class” (from 15 minutes before). Someone from Alimun may join to watch, and the trial class is recorded so we can review it; only Alimun staff can see the recording.

Once we have looked at how the trial went, we write to you with our decision. If you are approved, you get a “Welcome to Alimun” email and your full teacher dashboard opens. If we cannot approve your application, we tell you by email. You can add the times you are free to teach only after you are approved.

articles.subject: teachers
articles.title: How do I set my availability and get classes?
articles.summary: Add the times you are free each week under Classes, “Your availability”; you can then create a class inside those times, and rooms that fit what you can teach come to you as course contracts you may accept or decline.
body: On Classes, press “Your availability” to see your week. Under “Add free time”, choose the days (“Monday to Friday” and “Every day” are shortcuts), a start and an end, and press “Add”; “Add another time” adds a second block. Times are in the time zone of the device you use. Remove a block with “Remove”.

With your availability set, “Create a class” plans twelve weeks of classes for you. You choose the language, level, goal and plan, then the days, and the times offered are only those where a 60-minute class fits your free time in every one of the next twelve weeks. You can add a description that students see when they choose a class. You can have up to four open classes at a time. When a student joins one of your classes, you get an email with their name, level and goal.

Also on “Your availability”, “When you can teach” tells Alimun from when, at what time, in which language and at which levels you can teach, which kinds of classes (level packs, exam packs, open classes, help classes), and whether you can stand in as a substitute. Rooms are suggested from this and from the learners who are waiting.

Each room then comes to you as a separate course contract, shown on Classes under “Course contracts” and sent to you by email. The offer is made 10 days before the start if enough learners join, and gives the start date, days, time and number of learners, for 12 weeks. Press “Accept” or “Decline”; declining has no effect on the offers you get later. If a room does not get enough learners, we email you that it will not open.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: How do I cancel my plan?
articles.summary: Go to Settings in your dashboard and choose Manage billing; cancelling stops the next payment and you keep access until the end of the period you already paid for.
body: In your dashboard, go to Settings and choose Manage billing on your plan card. This opens Stripe's billing page, where you can cancel. You can also cancel by writing to us from Support in your dashboard, or by emailing support@alimun.com.

Cancelling stops the next renewal. You keep access until the end of the period you have already paid for, and your plan card in Settings then shows that your plan has been cancelled. The app and the open class can be stopped at any time this way. A level or exam pack paid monthly can be stopped before its next month, and you leave the room then.

Under the Terms, payments are not refunded for part of a period, unused classes or time you did not use, except where the law or the Terms say otherwise. If you live in the EU, the UK or another place with a legal right to withdraw from online contracts, you may also be able to withdraw from a recent purchase; see the article on refunds and withdrawal.

articles.subject: classes
articles.title: I can't join my class, or my camera or microphone is not working
articles.summary: Check the time, your plan and your browser's camera and microphone permission, then try Join again; if it still fails, write to us.
body: If the Join button is greyed out, the classroom is not open yet: it opens 15 minutes before the start and stays open until 90 minutes after. If the classroom could not open, a message under the video says why. "This session was cancelled" or "This session has already ended" means there is no class to join at that time. "You are not enrolled in this class" means your account does not have a place in it. "Your subscription is not active" means a payment did not go through: open Manage billing in Settings to update your card, then join again.

If you see "The classroom could not open. Try again, or come back closer to the start", reload the page and press Join again. The classroom runs in your browser, so a stable internet connection matters; closing other tabs and apps that use the camera or the connection can help.

If others cannot see or hear you, check that your browser is allowed to use your camera and microphone for alimun.com, that no other app is using them, and that they are not switched off in the video window. Then leave the classroom and join again.
If you still cannot get in, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com, with the class and the time, and the message you saw.

articles.subject: account
articles.title: I can't sign in, or I didn't get the password reset email
articles.summary: Check the message on the Sign in page, look in your spam folder for the reset email, and make sure you used the address of your account; if it still fails, write to us.
body: If the Sign in page says "The email or password is not right", check that you typed the address you signed up with, then reset your password with Forgot your password?. If it says "Please confirm your email first", open the confirmation link we sent when you created your account. If it says "Too many attempts right now", wait a few minutes and try again.

If the reset email does not arrive, wait a couple of minutes and look in your spam or junk folder for an email with the subject "Choose a new Alimun password". We only send it to an address that has an Alimun account, but the page shows the same message either way, so check that you typed the address of your account. Asking many times in a row does not help: after a few requests for the same address within an hour, no more emails are sent for a while.
If the link in the email says "This link has expired or was already used", press Request a new link and use the newest email. Each link works only once.

Teachers whose application is still being reviewed see "Your application is being reviewed" instead of their dashboard. If you still cannot get in, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com, from the address of your account if you can.

articles.subject: teachers
articles.title: I can’t start my class, or my students can’t see or hear me
articles.summary: Most problems come from opening the class too early, from being signed in with the wrong account, or from a video room that did not open the first time; the message on the classroom page tells you which.
body: If there is no “Start the class” button, it is probably too early: it appears 15 minutes before the start (10 minutes before for a 1:1). When the classroom cannot open, the page says “The classroom did not open.” followed by the reason, for example that the classroom opens 15 minutes before the session starts, that the session has already ended, or that it was cancelled.

If your dashboard shows a note saying it is a sample teacher, you are signed out or signed in with an account that is not your teacher account, and there is no real classroom. Sign in with the email address you teach with.

If the reason says the video room could not be created or video access could not be authorised, wait a moment and press “Start the class” again. If your students cannot see or hear you once you are in, leave the room and join again from the same button while the class is on.
If it still does not work, email support@alimun.com, or use “Contact us” in your dashboard, with the class and its time, and tell your students in the class conversation under Messages.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: My card was declined at checkout. What can I do?
articles.summary: The decision comes from your bank, so check with your bank or try another card with Use another card.
body: When the checkout says "Your bank declined the card.", the card was refused by your bank, not by Alimun. Nothing is charged when a card is declined. You can check with your bank and try again, or choose Use another card on the same page.
Some banks ask you to confirm a payment, for example in their app. When that happens the checkout opens your bank's check; finish it there and the payment goes through.
Moroccan cards need online international payments switched on, usually in your bank's app. Please also check your yearly allowance for payments abroad, then try again.

If the checkout says the payment did not go through and you do not know why, check your card details and try again. If it keeps failing, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com.

articles.subject: account
articles.title: How do I change the language of my dashboard?
articles.summary: Open Settings and choose a language under Dashboard language; it applies on the device you are using.
body: Open Settings in your dashboard and choose a language under Dashboard language. The dashboard reloads straight away in that language. You can choose English, Español, Français, Deutsch, Português, Italiano, 中文, العربية or Français (Maroc).
This changes the language of the buttons and explanations in your dashboard on this device. On another phone or computer, choose it there too.

Our emails to you are written in the language you use your dashboard in, so after you change it, new emails follow. This does not change the language you are learning, which is under About you in Settings.

articles.subject: account
articles.title: How do I change my name, email address or time zone?
articles.summary: Change your name and time zone in Settings under About you; your email address cannot be changed there, so write to us if you need a new one.
body: Open Settings in your dashboard. Under About you, change Your name, then press Save changes; you see "Saved." when it is done. Learners can also change their country, the language they are learning and their level there. Changing the language or level changes your book, practice and library, and the dashboard reloads.
In the student dashboard, Time zone is also under About you. Class times are shown in this time zone, so pick the one where you are and press Save changes.

Your email address is shown under Email, because it is the address you sign in with, but it cannot be changed in Settings. If you need to use a different address, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: How do I change my plan?
articles.summary: You add a new plan from Plans and prices in Settings, and you manage an existing subscription with Manage billing on your plan card in Settings.
body: In your dashboard, go to Settings. If you have a plan, your plan card has a Manage billing button, which opens Stripe's billing page, where you can change your card, see your invoices, change plan or cancel. The Plans and prices page also shows a Change your plan button that leads to the same place.

To add something new, such as a pack, voice practice minutes or a help class, choose it in Plans and prices. You cannot buy the same pack or subscription twice while you hold it; the checkout tells you "You already have this."

If you are in an open class and move up to a level or exam pack, you reserve the pack as usual. On the pack's first day your open class ends, and the part of the open-class month you had not used yet is taken off the pack's first payment, when both are in the same currency.
If something does not look right, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com.

articles.subject: classes
articles.title: My class was cancelled or moved, or my teacher is late
articles.summary: We tell you by email and on the bell in your dashboard when a class is cancelled or moved, and by email when your teacher is running late.
body: If a class is cancelled or moved to another time, we email you and show it on the bell in your dashboard, with the new time in your time zone and, when there is one, the reason. A moved class appears at its new time on your Classes page, and the classroom opens 15 minutes before the new start.

If your teacher has not arrived when the class should start, you may get an email saying your teacher is running a few minutes late and has been told. Please stay in the classroom or come back in a few minutes.

Schedules and teachers can change, for example when a teacher is unavailable. Under our Terms and Conditions, if we cancel a class and do not offer a replacement, we refund the unused part of your current billing period.
If you have questions about a cancelled class, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com.

articles.subject: teachers
articles.title: How do I write and publish the notes after a class?
articles.summary: Open the class date from Today or Classes, fill in the words and the grammar point, and press “Publish the notes”: your students see them in their dashboard, the words go into their flashcards and the class gets an email with the PDF.
body: Each class date has a notes page, which you open with “Prepare the notes” on Today, from the To do list once the class has ended, or with “Write the notes” under “The last four weeks” on Classes. You can also write in the Notes panel during the class. Everything you type is saved as a draft as you go.

The page has Words (up to ten, each with its meaning and an example sentence if you like), the grammar point and its explanation, what you did in class, the homework with its due date (the next class date unless you change it), and a note to the class. Only the grammar point is needed to publish; everything else is optional. Each word needs its meaning, or remove it.

Press “Publish the notes” when you are ready. Your students see the notes in their dashboard, the words go into their flashcards, and the class gets an email with the notes as a PDF, which you can open with “Open the PDF”. If you correct something later, press “Publish the changes”: students see the corrected notes, and nobody is emailed a second time.

After a 1:1, write your note with “Write the note” on Classes. Say what you worked on and what to do next; the student sees it in their dashboard. You can write it once the 1:1 has started, up to 4,000 characters.

articles.subject: classes
articles.title: Can I watch a recording of my class?
articles.summary: No, there are no class recordings for learners to watch; after each class you get your teacher's notes, the class words and the board instead.
body: Classes are live and are not made available as videos afterwards. What you keep from each class is on your Classes page: under Class notes, what your teacher wrote after the class (the grammar, the new words, what was done in class, the homework and a note from your teacher), with a PDF to download when your teacher adds one. You get a notification when the notes are ready.
The words from each class are added to your flashcards so you can review them, and you can open the board your teacher wrote on with See the board from this class.

As the classroom explains, Alimun records a few short moments of each group class, and Alimun staff may record a whole class if a concern is raised, to check quality and keep everyone safe. Only Alimun staff can see these recordings, and they are deleted after 30 days (90 days for a whole class). Teachers and learners cannot record.
Please do not record, photograph or screenshot a class, your teacher or other learners yourself without the consent of everyone shown. This is part of our Terms and Conditions.

articles.subject: teachers
articles.title: I can’t teach a class: how do I cancel or move it, and what are my students told?
articles.summary: Class dates are cancelled or moved by Alimun, not from the teacher dashboard, so write to us as early as you can; your students and you are then emailed the change.
body: There is no button in your dashboard to cancel or move a class date. If you cannot teach a class, email support@alimun.com, or use “Contact us” in your dashboard, as early as you can, with the class and the date.

When Alimun cancels or moves a class date, the class’s students and you normally get an email: “Session cancelled” or “Session moved”, with the old and the new time and the reason when one is given. For a moved class, the email says the classroom opens in the dashboard 15 minutes before the new start time. Cancelled dates disappear from your timetable.

If you are simply running late, join as soon as you can. If you are not in the room a few minutes after the start, Alimun may email you, and your learners may be told that you are running a few minutes late and are on your way.

articles.subject: classes
articles.title: Which time zone are my class times in?
articles.summary: Class times are shown in the time zone set in your Settings, or in your device's time zone if you have not set one.
body: Each class meets on fixed days at the same time every week, with the same teacher and the same group. The Classes page shows every time in your own time zone, and says which one at the top of the page ("Times in" followed by the zone).

The time zone comes from Settings, under About you, in the Time zone field. If you have not chosen one, the dashboard uses the time zone of the device you are on. If the times look wrong, for example after you move or travel, choose the right time zone there and press Save changes.

When you look at a class before joining it, the class's own time zone is shown beside your time if the two are different. The emails we send about your class, such as the one confirming your place or telling you a class has moved, also use your time zone when you have set one.

articles.subject: account
articles.title: Which cookies does Alimun use, and how do I change my choice?
articles.summary: Only the cookies needed to run the site are always on; analytics and marketing are used only if you accept them, and you can change your choice with Manage Cookies at the bottom of any page.
body: Some cookies and browser storage are strictly necessary: they keep you signed in, remember your cookie choices, your language and your currency, and protect payments against fraud. They cannot be switched off, because the site cannot work without them.

Analytics are used only if you accept them. Then we keep, in your browser, the website that sent you on your first visit, the page you arrived on and any campaign tags in the link, so we know how you found Alimun. We do not currently use marketing cookies.

When you first visit, the cookie banner lets you accept all, reject the ones that are not essential, or choose by category. You can change your choice at any time with the Manage Cookies link at the bottom of any page, or with Open Cookie Manager on the Cookie Policy page at alimun.com/cookies. If your browser sends a Global Privacy Control signal, we treat it as a refusal of marketing cookies.

articles.subject: tutor
articles.title: Does the tutor keep my conversations, and for how long?
articles.summary: Tutor conversations are kept for 90 days, recordings are never stored, and you can delete what the tutor remembers and every past session at any time.
body: The written conversation of each tutor session, including the transcript of a call, is kept for 90 days and then deleted automatically. Until then you can read it on the Tutor page under Your past sessions. Your voice recordings are never stored.

The tutor keeps a few notes about you between sessions, such as what you worked on, mistakes to keep an eye on and what to do next, so it can pick up where you left off. You can read them on the Tutor page under What your tutor remembers. Your teachers do not see your tutor sessions.

To delete everything, press Forget everything under What your tutor remembers, then Yes, forget everything. The tutor forgets what it remembers about you, and every past session and the practice it left for you are deleted. This cannot be undone.
The Privacy page at alimun.com/gdpr explains which AI providers receive what you write or say to the tutor and how long everything is kept.

articles.subject: account
articles.title: How do I get a copy of my data or delete my account?
articles.summary: Delete your account yourself with Delete your account in Settings, and email privacy@alimun.com for a copy of your data.
body: You can delete your account at any time. Open Settings in your dashboard and, under Your account, press Delete your account. We first show what you can do instead, such as cancelling your plan and keeping your progress. If you still want to go, type your email address to confirm. Your account is deleted straight away, any plan you pay for on alimun.com is cancelled, and we email you a confirmation. If you pay through the App Store or Google Play, cancel it there too. Teachers ask us through the Contact page, so that their classes and payouts are handed over.
If you pay for a plan, you can cancel it yourself with Manage billing in Settings, which opens the billing page where you can change your card, see your invoices, change plan or cancel.

To get a copy of the personal information we hold about you, in a format you can take elsewhere, email privacy@alimun.com. We check that the request comes from you and answer within one month, or sooner where the law requires it.

When an account is closed, its account, profile and learning data are deleted or anonymised within 90 days. Payment and invoice records are kept as long as tax and accounting law requires. If you only want the tutor to forget you, press Forget everything on the Tutor page: this deletes what the tutor remembers and every past tutor session.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: What happens when my paid period or my pack ends?
articles.summary: The app and the open class renew by themselves until you cancel, while a 12-week pack simply ends after its last paid month and nothing more is charged.
body: The app and the open class are subscriptions. They renew automatically for the same period, monthly or yearly, until you cancel. If a price goes up, we tell you by email at least 30 days before, and you can cancel before it takes effect.

A level, intensive or exam pack is 12 weeks. Paid monthly, it is three payments and then it stops by itself; paid upfront, the one payment covers the 12 weeks. Either way nothing more is charged when the pack is over. To keep learning with a teacher, choose your next pack or an open class in Plans and prices.
When nothing you have paid for is running any more, your account goes back to the free plan. Your book, practice and flashcards stay in your dashboard; classes with a teacher come with a plan.

articles.subject: dashboard
articles.title: How do I find my way around my dashboard?
articles.summary: Your dashboard is at alimun.com/app: the menu groups everything under Learn, With your teacher and Account, and Home shows your next class and what to do today.
body: Your student dashboard opens at alimun.com/app once you are signed in. On a computer the menu is on the left. On a phone the bar at the bottom has Home, Learn, Practice and Classes, and More opens the rest of the menu.

The menu has three groups. Learn holds Home, Course book, Practice, Flashcards, Tutor, Mock tests and Library. With your teacher holds Classes, Homework, Progress and Messages. Account holds Settings, where you change your profile and plan and choose what to keep on your device for offline use.

Home starts with Your next class, with a Join class button when it is time and See the calendar. Under it, Today’s plan shows what is due: flashcards to review, homework from your teacher or a topic from your level test, or Nothing due today when you are clear. Your focus topics shows what your level test pointed to, and Your tutor shows the tutor time you have left.

The Streak card counts the days in a row on which you did something: a lesson, a practice round or quiz, a flashcard review, a library piece, homework handed in or a live class. Until you have done something today it says Practise today to keep it going, and the week under it shows the days you were active.
The bell at the top of the screen holds your notifications.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: What is the founding price?
articles.summary: The founding price is a lower price on level, intensive and exam packs for the first 500 learners who join before 1 January 2027, kept for 12 months.
body: While founding places remain, the Plans and prices page and the checkout show the founding price on packs, together with the usual price. You get it by reserving or buying a pack before 1 January 2027 and while places are left; reserving with your card counts, even if your room starts and is charged later. If your room does not open, your founding price stays yours for another time or start date.

Your founding price is kept for 12 months. Before it ends we email you with the date. Nothing changes before then, and a pack you are already in keeps its price to its end. After that date, new purchases are at the usual price shown in Plans and prices.

articles.subject: classes
articles.title: I was invited to a free class with a new teacher. What is it?
articles.summary: It is a free 30-minute class given by a teacher who is joining Alimun; you can take a place, and afterwards tell us how it went with one tap.
body: Before a new teacher starts teaching at Alimun, they give a free 30-minute class to a few learners. When your language and level fit, you may see "You are invited to a free class" on your Classes page, with the day and time in your time zone.

Press Take a place to join, or No, thank you if it does not suit you. Once your place is saved, the class appears in your list on the Classes page and you join it from there, like any other class. If your plans change, use Give up my place so someone else can have it. If all places are taken, the page tells you.
The class is recorded so that Alimun can review the new teacher. Only Alimun staff watch the recording.

After the class you are asked "How was the class?" with three answers: Very good, Good and Not good. Tap one; your answer helps us choose our teachers. If a free class is cancelled, we email you, and you do not need to do anything.

articles.subject: tutor
articles.title: How do I get more tutor minutes?
articles.summary: You can buy a pack of 30 or 120 voice practice minutes once, which stay yours for 12 months, or choose a plan that adds minutes every month.
body: When your time is used up, the Tutor page shows "Your tutor time is used up", the date your plan's minutes come back if you have a plan, the plans with the minutes each one adds every month, and packs of minutes you can buy once. The packs are 30 or 120 minutes. The plans page in your dashboard also lists them under Voice practice minutes. The prices are shown there.

A pack is paid once through Stripe's secure checkout, not as a subscription. After paying you come back to the Tutor, and the minutes are added to your tutor time. It can take a minute: if your minutes do not show yet, open the Tutor again shortly. Bought minutes stay yours for 12 months from the purchase.
After you have spent a few minutes with the tutor, it asks how it is going and what we could improve. If you answer, we add extra minutes to your tutor time. This happens once.
If you paid and the minutes do not appear after a while, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com.

articles.subject: practice
articles.title: How do I hand in my homework?
articles.summary: Open Homework, choose the task, write or record your answer and press Hand it in; you can still change it until your teacher marks it.
body: Homework shows what your teacher has set, under To do, Waiting for your teacher and Marked. Each task shows its type and due date, and late ones say so. Press Start, or Continue if you have already begun, to open it.

For written homework, write your answer under The task. The word count shows how many words you have against your teacher’s minimum. Your draft is kept on this device as you type, so you can stop and come back to it on the same device. Press Hand it in and confirm with Yes, hand it in. If your text is shorter than your teacher asked, you are asked whether to hand it in anyway.

For speaking homework, record your answer, up to three minutes. Your words are written down and handed in as text, and the recording is not kept. Read what we heard and correct anything that was misheard before you hand it in.

Some homework is a lesson from your course book, a library piece or a mock test paper. Open it with the button on the task and finish it: it counts as handed in, with your score, as soon as you are done.

Once handed in, you can still change your answer until your teacher marks it: open it, edit it and press Hand in the new version. With a plan, Check before I hand it in gives you a few pointers on a written text of at least 15 words, drafted by AI; it does not rewrite your text or give a mark. If you are offline, your homework is kept on the device and handed in when you are back online.

articles.subject: practice
articles.title: Who marks my homework, and when do I see my mark?
articles.summary: Your teacher marks your homework; when they send the mark, it moves to Marked with a score out of 100 and their feedback, and a notification appears on the bell.
body: Your teacher marks the homework you hand in. While it waits, it is under Waiting for your teacher on the Homework page, and you can still change it.

When marking, your teacher can ask for a draft of the score and comments written by AI, then reads it, changes it as they see fit and sends it themselves. They can also mark without a draft. Nothing reaches you until your teacher sends the mark.

Once it is marked, the homework moves to Marked and a notification on the bell tells you. Press See the feedback to read Marked by your teacher, your score out of 100, your teacher’s comments and your own answer.

Homework that is a course book lesson, a library piece or a mock test paper is marked from your score as soon as you finish it. Lower on the Homework page, Feedback from your teacher holds the general notes your teacher writes about how you are doing. Marked written homework also counts towards your writing skill in Progress.

articles.subject: classes
articles.title: When does my class start, and what if it does not open?
articles.summary: A pack room opens on its start date once at least 8 learners have joined; until then nothing is charged, and if it does not open your reservation ends with nothing charged.
body: Group classes with a pack meet in a room: a fixed group with its own teacher, level, start date, days and time. A level pack is 12 weeks with three live classes a week, the intensive pack is 12 weeks with a class every weekday, and an exam pack is 12 weeks of classes that prepare you for the exam. When you choose a pack in Plans and prices, you see the rooms you can join with their start date, days, time, teacher and places left. An open class is one live class a week in a room of up to 20.

A pack room opens when at least 8 learners have joined. When you reserve, your card is saved and charged on the day your room opens, not before. You can also reserve without choosing a room and pick one when the next start dates are published; we email you when a room at your level is published. If no room is open at your level yet, press Tell me when a room opens and we email you once when one opens. Nothing is reserved or charged by that.

About ten days before the start date we look at each room. If a room is short of learners, it may join another room at the same level and start date so that it can open. If that happens we email you the new days and time, and if they do not suit you, reply to that email before the first day and we cancel your reservation.

If a room still does not have enough learners, it does not open. We email you, your reservation ends and nothing is charged. You can then choose another time or the next start date, and a founding price you had stays yours.

articles.subject: tutor
articles.title: How do my tutor minutes work, and what happens at the end of the month?
articles.summary: You get 10 free minutes once, a plan adds minutes every calendar month that do not carry over, and minutes you buy last 12 months.
body: Every new learner gets 10 free minutes with the tutor, given once, the first time you open the Tutor after confirming your email address. They are given once per email inbox. A plan adds more minutes every month; how many depends on your plan, and the Tutor page shows them. Under Time left you see your free minutes, your plan's minutes for this month with the date they are renewed, and any minutes added or bought.

Time is counted by our servers while you are in a session. Each turn counts the time since your previous turn, at least 5 seconds and at most 90 seconds, so stepping away does not use up your minutes, and a session with no turn for 10 minutes ends by itself. In a call, the time runs while the call is on; if nobody speaks for 2 minutes (5 while an exercise or a sentence to say is open), the tutor asks "Are you still there?" and the call then ends. If the tutor cannot answer a turn, the seconds of that turn are given back to you.

On a paid plan, written messages to the tutor do not use your minutes; instead there is a daily limit on written messages, and you can keep practising by voice when you reach it. Voice practice is limited to 30 minutes a day, whatever minutes you have left.

Your plan's minutes come first, then your free minutes, then minutes you bought, starting with those that expire soonest. Plan minutes are renewed on the first day of each month (UTC), and plan minutes you did not use do not carry over. Free minutes and bought minutes stay until you use them, except that bought minutes expire 12 months after the purchase. Minutes Alimun adds for you, for example as a thank-you for answering the short question about the tutor, do not expire. If your plan is no longer active, it stops adding minutes.

articles.subject: dashboard
articles.title: How do I install Alimun and use it offline?
articles.summary: In Settings, Use Alimun offline lets you put Alimun on your home screen and download your course book, library and mock tests to use without a connection.
body: Go to Settings and find Use Alimun offline. When your browser offers it, as on Android phones and in Chrome or Edge on a computer, press Install the app: Alimun goes on your home screen and opens full screen, straight to your course. On iPhone and iPad, open your dashboard in Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. Once it is installed, the card says Alimun is installed on this device.

In the same card you can download your course book, the book for your goal, the listening and reading of your course and the mock tests at your level, with their recordings. Press Download for one item or Download all for everything. Each download shows its size on the device, and Remove deletes it. The cover of your course book also has Download for offline.

Offline, your downloaded books, practice, flashcards and library still work, and your exercises are marked on your device. Your answers are kept and sent when you are back online, and a note tells you once they have been sent. Homework you hand in offline is handed in when the connection is back.
Live classes, the tutor, messages, progress and plans in Settings need a connection; while you are offline they say This needs a connection.

Without a plan, downloads hold the free parts only. When you take a plan, your downloads are completed the next time Alimun opens with a connection, and when a plan ends they go back to the free parts.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: How do I pay, change my card or find my invoices?
articles.summary: You pay by card through Stripe, and you change your card or see your invoices with Manage billing in Settings.
body: Payments on Alimun are handled by Stripe, and your card details never reach Alimun. At checkout you add a card first; if you want to pay with a different one, choose Use another card.

To change the card on your plan or see your invoices, go to Settings in your dashboard and choose Manage billing on your plan card. It opens Stripe's billing page, where you can change your card, see your invoices, change plan or cancel.
If you cannot find an invoice you need, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com.

articles.subject: classes
articles.title: How do I join my live class?
articles.summary: Open Classes in your dashboard and press Join, which opens 15 minutes before your class starts.
body: Your live classes are on the Classes page of your dashboard. The card at the top shows your next class, its day and time, your teacher and how long until it starts. The Join button is greyed out until the classroom opens, 15 minutes before the start, and the page tells you so.

When the classroom is open, press Join. The classroom opens inside your dashboard, in your browser, so there is nothing to install. You need a computer or another device with a camera, a microphone and a stable connection. If your browser asks whether the page may use your camera and microphone, allow it.

Beside the video there is a class panel with the chat and the words from the class. Anything you write in the chat is seen by the whole class. When your teacher opens the board, it appears next to the video.

You can still join if you are late: the classroom stays open until 90 minutes after the start. To join, you need an active plan that includes the class, or a trial or help-class place for that date. Use Add to my calendar on the same card to put the class in your own calendar.

articles.subject: classes
articles.title: How do I change class or leave my class?
articles.summary: Use Switch class or Leave the class on the Your class card in Classes; leaving gives your place to someone waiting and does not change your plan.
body: On your Classes page, the Your class card shows your class and teacher, with two buttons: Switch class and Leave the class.

Switch class opens Find a class, which lists the classes in your language that are taking students, with their days, time and teacher. Choose one and press Switch to this class. You leave your current class, and your place there goes to someone waiting. A class can only be joined if your plan includes it and it teaches the language set in your Settings. If a class is full, you can join its waiting list: when a place opens we email you, and the place is kept for you for 48 hours.

Leave the class asks you to confirm first. Your place goes to someone waiting, and your plan does not change, so leaving a class does not stop your payments. To change your plan or cancel it, use Manage billing in Settings. When you cancel, the next renewal stops and you keep access until the end of the period you have already paid for.

Rooms of the level, intensive and exam packs and of open classes are chosen in Plans and prices, not in Find a class. If you are in one of these rooms and want to move to another, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com.

articles.subject: teachers
articles.title: How do I use the prepared lessons and the board in class?
articles.summary: Each class date gets the next lesson Alimun has prepared for the course, which you can open, change or skip, and in the classroom the “Board” button shows that lesson’s pages to your students as you teach.
body: Alimun prepares the class lessons for each course, and you find them under Lessons. Each lesson has what the class is for, tips, a timed plan, the board pages (which you can try here as your students will see them), activities for 1 on 1, for 2 to 6 students and for 7 to 15 students, and the homework. Use them as they are or adapt them. Lessons marked “Being written” are not ready yet.

Every class date gets the next lesson of its course by itself. On the class date’s notes page, “Lesson for this class” shows it with “Open the lesson”. Under “Change the lesson” you can choose another lesson (the next classes then continue from there), “No prepared lesson” for that date, or “Next in the course” to go back to the usual order.

In the classroom, press “Board” to show the board beside the video; everyone sees the page you show. You can add a blank page, an empty page (lined, squared, two columns, a word map, a timeline or a table), the words from the last class or another page from the course. The tools are pen, highlighter, text, eraser, colour, undo and “Clear the page”. Exercise answers stay hidden until you press “Show the answers”.

Under “Who can write” you choose “Only me”, “Everyone” or one student. On an exercise page, “Everyone solves this” gives each student their own copy for the minutes you choose. They press “Show the teacher” when done, or their work comes to you when the time is up; you see who is working and who has sent, open anyone’s work, “Show to the class” if you like, and “End the exercise” to bring everyone back to the shared board.

The board saves itself during the class. Afterwards, the class date’s notes page shows “The board from this class” with your students’ own work. Tick “Students see the board with the class notes” if you want them to see it too.

articles.subject: practice
articles.title: What is in the Library?
articles.summary: Library has listening and reading pieces at your level, each with its words and exercises, and you can listen as often as you like.
body: Library shows the shelf for the language and level of your course. When your language has more than one level, you can switch level at the top of the page.

Listening pieces are conversations, announcements, interviews, talks and podcasts. Press Listen to play the recording as often as you like, or Slower to hear it more slowly. The transcript stays hidden until you press Show the transcript or finish the piece.
Reading pieces are notices, messages, articles, opinion pieces and stories. Tap a marked word to see what it means, and when the text has been recorded, Listen while you read reads it aloud to you.

Each piece comes with exercises that are checked straight away. Under Words from this piece, Add them to my flashcards puts its words into your flashcards in one tap. A finished piece counts for your streak and shows in Progress.
Without a plan, the first two texts of each shelf are open, and every library text comes with a plan. You can download your shelf, with its recordings, to use it offline.

articles.subject: dashboard
articles.title: How do I write to my teacher or my class?
articles.summary: Open Messages: each class you are in has a conversation with the whole class and one with just you and your teacher.
body: Open Messages, under With your teacher in the menu. For each class you are in, you have two conversations: one with your class, which everyone in the class and your teacher can read, and one that only you and your teacher can read.

Choose a conversation, type in Write a message and press Send. Messages are plain text. New messages appear while the conversation is open, and conversations with unread messages show how many are new.
If you see No conversations yet, you are not in a class yet; your conversations appear when you join one. Messages need a connection, so they are not available offline.

If a message is too long you are asked to split it in two, and if you send many messages very fast you are asked to wait a moment. For questions about your account, plan or payments, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com.

articles.subject: classes
articles.title: What happens if I miss a class?
articles.summary: Missed classes are not refunded or moved, but your teacher's notes, the class words and the board stay in your dashboard so you can catch up.
body: If you are only running late, you can still come in: the classroom stays open until 90 minutes after the start of the class.
If you miss a class completely, it is not refunded or rescheduled, unless your plan says otherwise. This is set out in section 4 of our Terms and Conditions.

You can still catch up. After each class your teacher writes notes, which appear under Class notes on your Classes page with the grammar, the new words, what was done in class and any homework, and you get a notification when they are ready. Where your teacher adds a PDF, you can download it. The class words are added to your flashcards, and you can open the board from that class with See the board from this class.

Until your next class you can also go over the lesson with your tutor, which recaps the grammar, practises the words and helps you prepare the homework. In the calendar, the classes you attended are marked "you were there".

articles.subject: practice
articles.title: How do the mock tests work?
articles.summary: Mock tests are full practice tests in the format of real exams, plus Alimun’s own end-of-level tests, taken one paper at a time and marked when you finish the paper.
body: Open Mock tests in the menu (Tests on a phone). Depending on your course you find practice tests in the format of B2 First, C1 Advanced, IELTS Academic, the Goethe-Zertifikat or telc Deutsch, and the Alimun test for your level. They are written by Alimun in each exam’s format; they are not official exam material, and Alimun is not affiliated with Cambridge English, IELTS, the Goethe-Institut or telc.

A test is made of papers, such as Reading, Writing, Listening and Speaking. Take them in any order, one at a time. Each paper has the time of the real exam, and you can tap the time to hide or show it; when time is up you can still finish your answers. You can leave a paper and come back to it, and your answers are kept on the device you are using until you finish it. In Listening, each recording can be played as often as the real exam allows.

Nothing is marked until you press Finish the paper, and you cannot change your answers after that. You then see every answer with its explanation, your score part by part and the transcripts of the recordings.

Writing and speaking answers get Drafted marks against the exam’s criteria, drafted automatically by AI as a guide, and every task shows a model answer. Pronunciation is not marked. Marking writing and speaking comes with a plan and has a daily limit; if you reach it, open the results again the next day to mark the rest. Your score is never turned into a predicted exam grade, and for Goethe and telc the page shows the pass mark the real exam publishes.
Without a plan, the first paper of each mock test is open and the other papers come with a plan.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: Should I pay for my pack monthly or upfront?
articles.summary: A level, intensive or exam pack is either three monthly payments or one payment for the 12 weeks that costs a little less, and either way your card is only charged once your room opens.
body: Level packs, the intensive pack and exam packs last 12 weeks. If you pay monthly, the first payment is taken on the day your room opens and then once a month, three payments in all. If you pay upfront, one payment for the whole 12 weeks is taken on the day your room opens, and it costs a little less than the three monthly payments together. The Plans and prices page shows both prices for your country.
A pack paid monthly can be stopped before its next month, and you leave the room then. A pack paid upfront is already paid for the full 12 weeks.

The other products have their own rhythm. The open class is paid monthly until you cancel. The app is paid monthly or yearly until you cancel. Help classes, the trial class and voice practice minutes are paid once, when you buy them.

articles.subject: account
articles.title: Which emails will I get, and how do I stop news and offers?
articles.summary: You always get emails about your account, classes and payments; news, offers and reminders come only if you are 16 or older and ask for them, and you can stop them in Settings or from any of those emails.
body: Emails about your account, your classes, your payments and changes to our terms are part of the service, so they are always sent. News, offers and reminder emails are different: we send them only to people who are 16 or older and ask for them.

To choose, open Settings in your dashboard and go to News and offers. Tick I am 16 or older, then tick or untick Send me news and offers from Alimun. Your choice is saved straight away and you see "Saved.". The second box can only be ticked once the first one is.

Every news, offers or reminder email also has a link at the bottom to stop them, which works without signing in, and the stop takes effect straight away. We keep a record of each choice you make, with its date, to show when you gave or withdrew your consent. The Privacy page at alimun.com/gdpr has the details.

articles.subject: dashboard
articles.title: What does the bell show?
articles.summary: The bell at the top of your dashboard shows your notifications: marked homework, changes to your classes, class notes, places offered to you, reminders and offers.
body: The bell at the top of your dashboard holds your notifications. A dot on it means something new, and opening it marks what it shows as read. Tap a notification to go to the page it is about.

You get a notification when your homework has been marked, when a place opens for you in a class (with the time it is held until), when one of your class sessions moves or is cancelled, and when the notes from a class are ready. Offers from Alimun can appear there too.

There are also a few reminders: when a week has gone by since you last practised, when you have taken the level test but not yet chosen a class or plan, and when your free tutor minutes are used up. If you agreed to receive news and offers, these reminders also come by email.
When there is nothing for you, the bell says Nothing new yet.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: My payment did not go through. What should I do?
articles.summary: Update your payment method from the email we sent you or with Manage billing in Settings, so your place in your class is kept.
body: When a monthly payment or the first-day payment of your pack fails, or your bank needs you to confirm it, we email you with an Update payment method button. In your dashboard, your plan card in Settings then says that your last payment did not go through. Use the button in the email, or go to Settings and choose Manage billing, to pay or change your card.

Your seat is held for a short time while you sort it out, and we try the payment again automatically in a few days. If it still cannot be taken, your access to live classes may be paused and your place in the room released, as the Terms allow, until the payment is made.
If your card was declined, see the article on declined cards. If you have updated your card and something still looks wrong, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: What plans can I choose from?
articles.summary: You can learn with a teacher in an open class, a level pack, an intensive pack or an exam pack, or use the app on its own, and you compare them all on the Plans and prices page.
body: The open class is one live class a week in a room of up to 20 people at your level, with the app included, and you can stop it whenever you like. The level pack is 12 weeks of three live classes a week with your teacher in a fixed room of up to 12 people, with the app included. The intensive pack is the same idea with a live class every weekday, Monday to Friday, for 12 weeks, and it is for English only. The exam pack is 12 weeks of live classes that prepare you for IELTS in English, or for Goethe or telc B1 in German, with three mock exams marked by your teacher and the app included. Alimun prepares you for the exam; the certificate is issued by the exam board.

The app on its own gives you every unit, the full course book, exercises and 60 minutes of voice practice a month, paid monthly or yearly. You can also buy a 30-minute help class in a small group on the week's units, a trial class (one live class in a running room, once per person), and extra voice practice minutes for the tutor, which are yours for 12 months.

To compare them, open the Plans and prices page on alimun.com (alimun.com/tiers), where you can switch between English and German. Inside your dashboard, go to Settings and choose See the plans, or open Plans and prices from there. Prices are shown for the country you are in, and the country your card was issued in sets the final price, which you always see before anything is charged.

articles.subject: practice
articles.title: How does Practice work, and why do my mistakes come back?
articles.summary: Practice gives you short rounds and quizzes from the units of your course book you have reached, and the answers you got wrong come back first until you know them.
body: A quick round is six exercises from the units of your course book you have reached, mixed in new ways so the same item rarely looks the same twice. Press Start a round on the Practice screen. A finished round counts for your streak.

The Your mistakes card shows how many answers are waiting for you. Anything you get wrong in a lesson, a unit test, a quiz or a round comes back first in your next rounds, and each time you get it right it waits a little longer before it comes back again. Items you have not seen yet come after your mistakes.

Under Quizzes you find Beat the clock, 90 seconds to give as many right answers as you can, a Mixed quiz of 15 questions from every unit you have reached, and, Unit by unit, a 12-question Quiz or a Long practice set with help along the way. Quizzes are checked at the end, your best score is kept, and the questions you missed come back in your rounds.

There is also a Listening round with the voices of your course book once its recordings are ready, and Speaking, where you pick your tutor, listen and then say the sentences yourself; your recording is turned into text by speech recognition, compared word by word and not kept. Every kind of exercise lets you try each type of exercise once: the first three kinds are free and every kind comes with a plan. Sets your teacher sends you appear under From your teacher, with Do it again and Just my mistakes.
When you are signed in, your practice is saved to your account. Without an account it is kept in that browser only.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: Why does my price depend on my country, and which currency do I pay in?
articles.summary: Prices follow the cost of living in each country, the country your card was issued in sets your final price, and you see the exact amount before anything is charged.
body: The prices on the Plans and prices page are shown for the country you are in at the moment. At checkout you add your card first, and the country that card was issued in sets your final price and currency. The page then tells you, for example, "Your card is from France, so your price is" followed by the amount, before anything is charged. That price is held for 15 minutes; after that you are asked to add your card again.

You pay in your country's currency where we offer it: euros, pounds, Swiss francs, US, Canadian and Australian dollars or Moroccan dirhams. Otherwise you pay in euros or US dollars. Prices include tax, except in the United States and Canada, where sales tax is added at checkout where it applies.

Once you have paid, your price level stays with your account. If you later pay with a card from a country with higher prices, the higher price applies straight away. A card from a country with lower prices changes your price level only after 90 days.

articles.subject: dashboard
articles.title: My progress or my homework is missing. What can I do?
articles.summary: Check that you are signed in and online, and open Alimun on the device where you did the work: drafts, unfinished mock papers and anything done offline wait there until they are sent.
body: First make sure you are signed in to the account you used. If Home says Your data could not be loaded, so Home shows sample data for now, your own data did not arrive: check your connection and press Try again. Progress needs a connection to load.

Some things stay on the device where you did them until they are sent. A homework draft you have not handed in yet and the answers of a mock test paper you have not finished are kept in that browser, so open them on the same device. Answers and homework given while offline are sent when that device is back online, so open Alimun there with a connection. Without an account, your progress is kept in that browser only.

Homework appears for the classes you are in. Homework that is a course book lesson, a library piece or a mock test paper counts as handed in once you finish it; open Homework again and it is recorded.
In Progress, a skill says not enough answers yet until enough of your answers have been counted, so a new skill can look empty at first.
If something is still missing, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com, and tell us what is missing and on which device you did it.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: I was charged and want a refund. Can I get one?
articles.summary: Payments are not refunded except where the law or the Terms say so, but if you live in the EU or the UK you can withdraw from a purchase within 14 days from Settings in your dashboard.
body: Under the Terms, payments are not refundable, and there are no refunds or credits for part of a period, unused classes or time you did not use, except where the law requires it or the Terms say otherwise. If we cancel a class and do not offer a replacement, or we end your plan for a reason other than a breach of the Terms, we refund the unused part of your current billing period. The same applies if we change the service in a way that significantly reduces what you paid for and you choose to cancel.

If you live in the EU or the EEA, you can withdraw from a purchase within 14 days of buying it, without giving a reason. In your dashboard, go to Settings and choose Withdraw from contract here on your plan card, pick the purchase, check your details and choose Confirm withdrawal. We email you a confirmation with the date and time. We refund what you paid within 14 days, to the payment method you used. If you asked for classes to start during the withdrawal period, the classes already given are deducted. If the purchase is a subscription, we end it for you.

People living in the UK have the same 14-day right. In Morocco the right to withdraw from a distance contract is 7 days, and in Australia the guarantees of the Australian Consumer Law apply. You can also withdraw by email to legal@alimun.com.

A reserved pack whose room does not open is never charged, so there is nothing to refund. For any other question about a charge, write to us from Support in your dashboard, or email support@alimun.com.

articles.subject: plans
articles.title: What does it mean to reserve a place in a pack?
articles.summary: When you reserve a place in a level, intensive or exam pack, your card is saved but nothing is charged until the day your room opens, and if the room does not open you are not charged at all.
body: In your dashboard, go to Settings, then Plans and prices, and choose a pack. You see the rooms on offer with their start date, days, time and the real number of places left, and you pick one with Choose. You then add your card and see your exact price, and Reserve my seat saves your place. Nothing is charged that day: your card is charged on the day your room opens, either once for the 12 weeks or once a month for three months, depending on how you chose to pay.

A room opens when at least 8 learners join. If not enough people join, the room does not start, your reservation ends and nothing is charged. We email you, and you can choose another time or the next start date.

If no room suits you yet, you can choose Reserve without choosing a room and pick your room when the next start dates are published. When a room at your level is published we email you, and on the same page you choose Move my reservation here. If you would rather not reserve anything yet, Tell me when a room opens sends you one email when a room at your level opens; nothing is reserved or charged.

articles.subject: teachers
articles.title: How do I set and mark homework?
articles.summary: Set homework under Homework with “Set homework”, then mark each piece yourself: you can ask for an AI-drafted mark and feedback, but nothing reaches the student until you have checked it and pressed “Send to the student”.
body: Under Homework, press “Set homework” and choose a class or one student. It can be a task to write or say, a course book lesson, a library piece or a mock test paper. For a task you give a type, a title, the task itself and, if you like, a minimum number of words; “Draft a task for me” uses AI to write a task from a topic, in the language and at the level of your students, and fills the form for you to change. Students see the homework in their dashboard straight away. A book lesson, library piece or mock paper is marked by itself, with the score of the student’s answers.

Homework handed in waits on Homework, oldest first. Open a piece with “Mark” to see the task and the student’s answer, or, for spoken homework, what the student said. You can mark it entirely yourself: give a mark out of 100 (students see it as a percentage) and write your feedback.

If you want help, press “Draft the feedback”. An AI model reads the task and the student’s work and suggests a mark with feedback: an overall view, what went well, what to work on next and one corrected sentence. It fills the form only. Read it, change the mark and the words as you see fit, and press “Send to the student”; until then nothing is sent. You can change a mark later and press “Send the changes”. “Next to mark” takes you to the next piece.

On a piece of homework you have set, you see who has handed it in, who is late and who has not yet, and you can change it with “Save the changes”. You can delete it only while nobody has handed it in.

Under Material you can make your own exercise sets for a class or one student, write the exercises yourself or have AI draft three at a time from a topic, a text or your students’ mistakes, check them with “Try it”, and send them. A set you send appears in the student’s Practice, and you can also set it as homework, marked by itself from their score. Your sets stay private to you until you send them.

articles.subject: account
articles.title: How do I sign in, and how do I reset my password?
articles.summary: Sign in with your email and password; if you forgot the password, use Forgot your password? on the Sign in page and follow the link we email you.
body: Sign in on the Sign in page with the email address and password of your account. Learners and teachers use the same page.

If you forgot your password, press Forgot your password? on the Sign in page, enter the email address of your account and press Send the link. We email you a link to choose a new password; in English its subject is "Choose a new Alimun password". It can take a minute or two to arrive. Open it, type your new password twice and press Save the new password. The link works once and only for a limited time; if it has expired, press Request a new link. Saving a new password signs you out on your other devices.
If you know your password and want to change it, open Settings in your dashboard and go to Your account. Type the new password under New password and press Change password.
A password needs at least 8 characters, with a lowercase letter, a capital letter and a number. To sign out, press Sign out in the same Your account card.

articles.subject: tutor
articles.title: How do speaking practice and pronunciation checks work, and how do I allow the microphone?
articles.summary: You speak to the tutor or record sentences in Practice, an AI turns your voice into text or scores your pronunciation, and your recordings are never kept.
body: With the tutor, press Speak, say what you want (up to about 30 seconds) and press Stop and send; your words appear as your message. Sometimes the tutor puts a sentence on the board under Say this sentence aloud. Press Say it, read it out, and an AI pronunciation check scores how you said it: words in green were said well, words underlined in coral were said a little differently, and you see your accuracy, fluency and completeness. Hear it slowly plays the sentence slowly, and the tutor asks you to try again until it is right.

In Practice, Speaking lets you pick your tutor, listen, then tap Record and say each sentence. Your recording is turned into text by AI and compared with the sentence. Speaking practice comes with a plan, has a daily limit that resets at midnight UTC, and does not use your tutor minutes.

The first time you speak, your browser asks whether Alimun may use your microphone: choose Allow. If you refused by mistake, allow the microphone for alimun.com in your browser's site settings and reload the page. In a call you can press Mute at any time. Calls need a recent Chrome, Safari, Edge or Firefox; if yours cannot make the call, you can always write to your tutor instead. If nothing was heard, speak a little closer to the microphone.

Your recordings are never stored. They are sent to our AI providers only to turn them into text (Groq) or to score your pronunciation (Microsoft Azure, servers in the European Union), and are then discarded; for pronunciation we keep only the scores. In a live call your voice goes to Google's Gemini API to hold the call, and the audio is not stored.

articles.subject: teachers
articles.title: How do I check in and start my live class?
articles.summary: Check in on Today from an hour before your class, at least 5 minutes before it starts, then press “Start the class” from 15 minutes before to open the classroom in your dashboard.
body: From an hour before your class, Today shows “Check in”. Please check in at least 5 minutes before the start, so we know you are there; Today then shows the time you checked in. You may also get reminder emails an hour and 5 minutes before the class, with a “Check in” button and an “Open the classroom” button.

“Start the class” appears 15 minutes before the start, on Today and on Classes. It opens the classroom inside your dashboard: the video call, the “Board” button, and a side panel with Chat (the class conversation, which everyone in the class can read), Notes (your notes for this class, saved as you type) and Words (the words from the last class, when there were any). On a phone the side panel opens from a button. If you leave by mistake, you can join again from the same button while the class is on.

In the room you can mute or remove participants. Nobody can record from the room, teachers and learners included. Alimun records a few short moments of each group class, and Alimun staff may record a whole class if a concern is raised; the classroom shows this notice.

If you are not in the room a few minutes after the start, Alimun may email you and tell your learners that you are on your way. For a 1:1, “Join” opens 10 minutes before and the room stays open until 15 minutes after the 1:1 ends.

articles.subject: teachers
articles.title: How do I follow my students’ progress and message them?
articles.summary: Students shows each class and each student from what they actually do between classes, with those who need attention first, and Messages holds one conversation per class and a private one per student.
body: Students lists the students of your classes, class by class, with those who need attention first: a student who has not practised for 7 days, has missed the last two classes, or has homework past its due date that is not handed in.

Open a class with “See the class” to see who came to class over the last eight weeks, where the class struggles (the course book lessons with the most wrong answers in practice), how far each student is in the course book, and the homework with its marks. Open a student to see the same figures they see on their own Progress page, their homework with marks, and the notes about them.
You can add a note to a student. Students can read a note in their dashboard, unless you tick “Private”: then only teachers and Alimun see it.

Messages has one conversation per class you teach, which everyone in that class can read, and a private conversation with each student, which only you and that student can read. To start one, choose the student under “Write to a student”; “Message” on a student’s page also takes you to Messages. Messages are plain text. If a message is too long, split it in two; if you send very fast, wait a moment and try again. Unread messages also show on Today.

articles.subject: teachers
articles.title: Where do I change my profile, and where do I see what I have been paid?
articles.summary: Settings holds your name, location, specialty and the bio students read, plus your password and the dashboard’s language; Payouts shows each payout Alimun has recorded for you and what you have taught this month.
body: Under Settings, “About you” has your name, where you teach from, what you specialise in, the country you live in, and “About you, for students”: a few sentences students read when they choose a class. Press “Save changes” to keep them. Your email is the address you sign in with and is shown but cannot be changed here. The languages you teach are set by Alimun; to change them, write to us.

Settings also lets you choose the dashboard’s language on this device, change your password (at least 8 characters, with a lowercase letter, a capital letter and a number), turn news and offers from Alimun on or off, and sign out. To delete your account, use “Ask us to delete your account”.

Payouts shows this month so far: the classes taught and the 1:1s completed, per class. It shows counts only; your payout is worked out by Alimun at the end of each period. Below, each payout Alimun has recorded for you is listed with its period, the number of classes, the amount in euros and its state: “Paid” with the date, “Being paid”, or “Not paid yet, Alimun is looking into it”.
If you have a question about a payout, press “Contact us” on the Payouts page, or email support@alimun.com.

articles.subject: teachers
articles.title: What is on my teacher dashboard?
articles.summary: Your teacher dashboard at alimun.com/app/teach opens on Today, with your next class and what needs doing, and has sections for your classes, students, homework, lessons, material, messages, payouts and settings.
body: Your teacher dashboard is at alimun.com/app/teach. On a computer the sections are in the menu on the left, grouped as Teaching (Today, Classes, Students, Homework), Create (Lessons, Material) and Account (Messages, Payouts, Settings). On a phone, Today, Classes, Students and Homework are in the bar at the bottom, and the other sections are under “More”.

Today shows your next class with its day, time and number of students. From an hour before it you can press “Check in”, and from 15 minutes before “Start the class” opens your classroom. “Prepare the notes” takes you to that class’s notes page.

Below it, To do lists what is waiting for you: notes to write for classes that have ended, homework to mark (the student who has waited longest first), unread messages and notes to write after 1:1 follow-ups. When everything is done it says “All caught up”. You also see the next seven days, your classes with how many places are taken, and the homework that has waited longest. Today refreshes itself every few minutes while it is open.

articles.subject: dashboard
articles.title: Where can I see my progress?
articles.summary: Progress shows your level, your skills, your lessons and your weeks, counted only from what you have actually done.
body: Open Progress, under With your teacher in the menu. Everything on it is counted from what you have done; nothing is estimated.

At the top you see your course level, the level your level test placed you at, how many course book lessons you have done and unit tests you have passed, and how many words you have learned out of your flashcards.

Skills shows the share of your answers that were right in listening, speaking, reading, writing, and grammar and words, from practice, the library, mock tests and marked homework, and says what each one is based on. When there are not enough answers yet, it says so instead of showing a number.

Lessons to work on and Your strongest lessons point to course book lessons, with Practise these. Your weeks shows the days you practised, read, took a class or handed in homework in each of the last twelve weeks, and Lately lists what you finished recently. Sessions with your tutor lists your latest sessions with the tutor.
Progress needs a connection. When you are offline it says This needs a connection and opens again when you are back online.

articles.subject: classes
articles.title: What are the trial class and the help class?
articles.summary: The trial class is one live class in a group that is already running, once per person; the help class is a 30-minute live class in a small group on the week's units.
body: Both are single classes that you buy once, from Plans and prices in your dashboard (in Settings, under See the plans). Instead of choosing a group, you choose a class date: the page lists the times that are open, in your time zone, with the real number of places left. A date has to be at least an hour away to be booked.
The trial class lets you take part in one live class of a group that is already running, so you can see what a class with a teacher is like before you choose a plan. It can be taken once per person.
The help class is a 30-minute live class in a small group, on the units of the week.

Once you have paid, the class appears on your Classes page and you join it like any other class, with the Join button that opens 15 minutes before the start. Your place is for that one date only. The price depends on the country your card was issued in, and you see the exact amount before anything is charged.

articles.subject: account
articles.title: What data does Alimun keep about me, and for how long?
articles.summary: We keep what we need to run your account and your learning, for as long as your account is open, and the Privacy page lists everything and how long it is kept.
body: We keep your account details (name, email address, the language you learn or teach, your level and your preferences, your country and whether you confirmed you are 16 or older), your learning (test results, classes, attendance, homework, scores, feedback, flashcards and practice), your plan and payments, and messages you send us. Card numbers are entered on Stripe's pages; we never store them. We also record which parts of your dashboard you open and what you do there, but for messages we record only that you sent one, not what it said. Alimun does not record live classes.

Your account, profile and learning data are kept while your account is open and deleted or anonymised within 90 days after you close it. Tutor conversations are kept for 90 days. The record of which parts of your dashboard you open is deleted after 24 months, and dashboard notifications after 12 months. Payment and invoice records are kept as long as tax and accounting law requires.

We never sell your personal information. We share it only as needed to run Alimun: your teacher sees your profile, work and progress, and companies that work for us, such as our database host, Stripe for payments, our video and email services and our AI providers, process it on our instructions.
The Privacy page at alimun.com/gdpr lists everything in full, including your rights. For any question about your data, email privacy@alimun.com.

articles.subject: tutor
articles.title: What is the tutor, and is it a real person?
articles.summary: The tutor is an AI practice tutor in your student dashboard: it is a computer program, not a person, and a teacher does not review its sessions.
body: The Tutor in your student dashboard is an AI tutor. You are talking to a computer program that uses artificial intelligence, not to a person. It explains on a whiteboard, sets exercises where you need them most, listens to you, speaks, and remembers what you did together. Its sessions are not reviewed by a teacher.

You can write to your tutor with Write to your tutor, speak to it with Speak, or, where the call is available, choose one of the tutors under Talk with your tutor and talk to them like on a call. Each tutor has their own voice. When your teacher has published the notes of a class, you can also go over that lesson with your tutor from Home or Classes.
At the end of a session the tutor writes a short summary, adds the session's words to your flashcards and leaves practice for you in Practice, under From your tutor.

Like any AI, the tutor can make mistakes, so do not rely on it alone for an important decision. Your live classes with a teacher stay at the heart of your course. To produce the tutor's replies, what you write or say is sent to AI providers that work for Alimun (Groq for the replies, Google for the tutor's voice and the live call, Microsoft Azure for pronunciation scores). The Privacy page at alimun.com/gdpr explains this in full. Learners under 16 may use the tutor only with a parent's authorisation.

articles.subject: dashboard
articles.title: How does my course book work?
articles.summary: Course book takes you through your course unit by unit: each lesson teaches on a few pages and checks you with exercises, and every unit ends with a unit test you pass with 70%.
body: Open Course book in the menu (Learn on the bottom bar of a phone). You see the book for your course and level, its units and where you left off, with Start or Continue. Each unit has lessons, and each lesson is a few pages that you turn like a book: a page explains something, then checks it with exercises.

Exercises in lessons are checked as soon as you answer. If an answer is wrong you can try again, and after two wrong tries Show the answer appears. The next page opens when the exercises on the page you are on are done.

Every unit ends with a Unit test. Nothing is marked until you check the whole test at the end, and you need 70% to pass and finish the unit. If you do not pass yet, go back over the lessons and take it again; your best score is kept. Answers you get wrong in lessons and tests come back later in your practice rounds.

Explanations are in the language your dashboard is set to, where the book has it. The Explanations switch lets you read them in the language you are learning instead; example sentences, exercises and texts are always in the language you are learning. Some courses also have A second book for your goal, with real situations for what you want to do with the language.

Without a plan, the first three units of each book are open, and the rest shows Comes with a plan; any paid plan opens the whole book. Units that are still being written show Being written and open as soon as they are ready.
